candidates.description: At the entry fork, commit the delve to the WEST. This opens the western path (a forge, then a vault beyond it) and seals the eastern path forever. The west is more work -- you must breach the forge for its key before the vault will open -- but the vault yields a sigil, the richer prize.

At the entry fork, commit the delve to the EAST. This opens the eastern path (a hall, then a spur beyond it) and seals the western path forever. The east is easier -- a straight hall to a spur -- but the spur is only a relic in a dead end, a lesser prize than the western vault's sigil.
Breach the western forge. Produces a gold key (needed by the vault) and clears the way to the vault beyond. Reachable only if the delve was forked west.
Breach the western vault, yielding its sigil. Requires both the forge cleared (to reach it) and the gold key (from the forge).
Breach the eastern hall, clearing the way to the spur beyond. Reachable only if the delve was forked east.
Breach the eastern spur, yielding its relic. A dead end -- nothing lies beyond it.

jev.instructions: You are delving a dungeon the cannon has laid out. At the entry, a single fork forces one irreversible choice: WEST (harder -- a forge whose key opens a vault holding a sigil) or EAST (easier -- a hall to a spur holding only a relic). Choosing one seals the other path forever. After the fork, breach the rooms of the chosen path in whatever order their requirements allow. There is no single correct delve -- weigh the richer western prize against the easier eastern one.
